sanskrit: कार्यकारणकर्तृत्वे हेतुः प्रकृतिरुच्यते । पुरुषः सुखदुःखानां भोक्तृत्वे हेतुरुच्यते ॥
hindiTranslation: प्रकृति और पुरुष  दोनोंको ही तुम अनादि समझो और विकारों तथा गुणोंको भी प्रकृतिसे ही उत्पन्न समझो ।  कार्य और करणके द्वारा होनेवाली क्रियाओंको उत्पन्न करनेमें प्रकृति हेतु कही जाती है और सुखदुःखोंके भोक्तापनमें पुरुष हेतु कहा जाता है ॥
englishTranslation: Nature is said to be the cause of the body, the senses, and action. The inner being is said to be the cause of experiencing pleasure and pain.
essence: Action belongs to nature; experience belongs to the one who knows.
speaker: Krishna
simpleMeaning: The body, senses, and actions belong to nature. Pleasure and pain are experienced by the inner being. Krishna separates the changing process from the one who experiences it.
simpleInsight: You can stop confusing what happens with who you are.
detailedMeaning: Krishna explains that nature drives bodily action, while the inner being only experiences pleasure and pain. This distinction prepares Arjuna to act without mistaking himself for the moving field.
modernRelevance: Before a court hearing, a man's stomach knots and his hands sweat on their own. Krishna would place the body's reaction in prakriti, and the experiencing of that fear in Purusha.
translationLiteral: कार्यकारणकर्तृत्वे (in the doership of body, senses, and action) / हेतुः (cause) / प्रकृतिः (nature) / उच्यते (is said) । / पुरुषः (the inner being) / सुखदुःखानाम् (of pleasure and pain) / भोक्तृत्वे (in the state of experiencer) / हेतुः (cause) / उच्यते (is said)
insight: Prakriti causes the body, senses and action, Krishna says, while Purusha is the cause of experiencing pleasure and pain.
